correctness.rationale: For all p,q>=3 and a,b,c>0, the nonbridge twin spaces force p-2 and q-2 coordinate inputs. With exactly these controls, zero coordinates at selected vertices impose bridge values -u,-v, leaf equations (ap-lambda)u=(bq-lambda)v=0, and the bridge equation c(u-v)=0. Hence the only invisible eigenvector is the explicit one-dimensional plus/minus mode, occurring iff ap=bq; each of its four remaining coordinates is nonzero. PBH then proves the necessary-and-sufficient criterion for every control set. Zero forcing is independently characterized using twin obstructions and explicit forcing. The polynomial and counts follow by finite binomial counting. The standalone script replays 37704 checks over 36 finite weighted cases, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Searches of published mathematical records and primary literature did not reveal the same if-and-only-if vertex-set criterion for weighted two-clique barbells. A published record already determines the zero-forcing polynomial, which is treated solely as comparison/background; the newly assessed content is the sharp fixed-Laplacian resonance ap=bq, all independent-terminal-input controllable sets, and the exact equality/difference with zero forcing. Path/cycle, grid, broadcast-input, and single-input composite-graph results have different domains and do not imply these weighted multi-input statements. Unindexed alternative formulations remain possible.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by choosing few independent actuators in a network of two densely coupled communities connected by a bottleneck. The complete leader-set classification reveals a sharp internal-rate spectral resonance independent of the bridge strength: at ap=bq all zero-forcing sets and only those are controllable, but off resonance (p-1)(q-1) smaller, non-zero-forcing configurations work. It gives explicit sharp actuator counts, every valid placement, and an exact enumerator; those are structural design rules and not a renaming or isolated parameter substitution. The comparison to the already known zero-forcing polynomial is explicitly separated from the assessed contribution.
